newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican blown apart by own bomb.
newsitem.headline: Corsican blown apart by own bomb.

text.p: A 24-year-old Corsican man was blown apart on his birthday by a bomb he was carrying outside his parents' home, police said on Monday.

Don Marc Tomasi, born on March 2, 1973, was killed late on Sunday near the north Corsican town of Bastia. His parents were inside the house at the time and were unable to explain why their son was carrying the homemade bomb.
Police said Tomasi was not a known political activist or criminal.
Both Corsican separatists and local criminals set off hundreds of bombs every year on this turbulent Mediterranean island to further political aims or as part of extortion attempts.
The attacks are nearly always at night against empty premises and aimed at avoiding casualties. Bombers are rarely injured in accidents as weapons-happy Corsicans are often specialists in explosives.
The last bomb attack on the island was on Friday in the southern town of Porticcio, destroying a restaurant but causing no injuries.
No-one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast, but suspicion centred on separatists waging a two-decade-long guerrilla campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France.
